name: SkillEvaluator
description: Multi-tier framework for evaluating AI agent skills with quality gates, semantic overlap detection, synthetic evaluation dataset generation, and live agent evaluation that measures how skills affect agent behavior.
one_liner: A grading tool that checks whether an 'AI skill' add-on (instructions that teach an AI assistant a new trick) is actually well-written and genuinely helps, before you trust it or publish it.
buyer: A company building or curating a marketplace of AI agent skills who needs an objective quality bar before publishing third-party skills to customers.
business_use_cases: A plugin marketplace runs every submitted skill through it automatically and rejects low-quality or duplicate submissions before they go live.
An enterprise AI platform team uses it in CI to make sure internal skill updates don't silently make their AI assistants worse.
A skill-authoring consultancy uses the scoring reports as proof of quality when selling custom skills to clients.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a hosted 'skill certification' badge service: pay a small fee to have your skill scanned and certified before listing it in a marketplace
Sell CI integration support/consulting to companies building internal skill libraries

steal_this: It's a narrow dev-tooling niche with a thin market today — mostly useful to the handful of teams building skill marketplaces. A 'skill certification' micro-service is the most buildable angle, but demand is small right now.
